subject: Urban Planning
title: Smart Grids: Electricity That Thinks
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Smart Grids: Electricity That Thinks.

hook.text: A smart grid knows when your neighborhood is using too much power and reroutes electricity in milliseconds.

buildup.text: Traditional grids push power one way — from plant to home. Smart grids are two-way: your solar panels feed back in.

discovery.text: Smart meters let consumers see real-time usage and shift demand to off-peak hours, saving money and carbon.

twist.text: Texas's grid collapsed in 2021 because it wasn't connected to neighboring states. Smart within, isolated without.

climax.text: Vehicle-to-grid technology lets parked EVs supply power during peak demand. Your car becomes a battery.

punchline.text: The grid that talks back. Your house sells power to your neighbor.

quiz.question: What makes a smart grid different from a traditional power grid?
options: It uses nuclear power exclusively instead of fossil fuels
It allows two-way power flow and real-time demand management
It operates underground instead of using overhead power lines
